issues.detail: Covers the happy path and some cost/loop warnings, but gives no troubleshooting for common failures such as missing API keys, rate-limit errors, tool failures, or hierarchical-process misconfiguration.
Examples are brief prose descriptions that point back to the code blocks, and Example 2 relies on an undefined run_readonly_query function with no sample data or output.

scenarios.name: scaffold-and-run-crew-project
scenarios.rationale: B hits every rubric item explicitly (create/install/run, YAML files plus @CrewBase in crew.py, kickoff(inputs=...), provider key in .env with don't-commit), while A is more detailed and mostly correct but never mentions @CrewBase or the don't-commit warning, and its crewai install/run steps come after a cd into research_crew instead of the hyphenated dir named in the rubric flow.

scenarios.name: researcher-writer-crew-with-context
scenarios.rationale: Both responses satisfy every rubric item (two Agents with role/goal/backstory, two Tasks with expected_output, context=[research_task], output_file, Process.sequential, kickoff(inputs=...), printing result.raw and result.token_usage), but A has a bug: its researcher goal is an f-string with {{topic}} that renders as {topic}, which works yet is needlessly convoluted, while A adds a TOPIC constant and a detailed token breakdown; B is more concise and matches the rubric directly, with a minor unverified claim about checks against crewai 1.15.23.

scenarios.name: custom-readonly-sql-tool-with-safeguards
scenarios.rationale: Both subclass BaseTool with an args_schema Pydantic model and a string-returning _run, attach it to an agent with allow_delegation=False, max_iter and max_rpm, and advise read-only DB access and input validation. B is stronger: it gives a concrete read-only role, sqlglot validation, a per-run call cap, an output cap and max_execution_time. A is thinner, and it never defines run_readonly_query. Neither response sets allow_code_execution explicitly, but A at least mentions keeping it off and B does not mention it at all, a small gap for B. B's depth outweighs this.
